gen-fs-expose-gf-nokora: Nokora has a wide-open s and a dark, thick stripe of lowercase. Expose sits above it, compressed and striking, with barely any gap between its small letters and its capitals, so each line lands with very little pause.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Expose is striking and refined, packing its capitals tight against the lowercase and moving with hardly a pause. Noto Kufi Arabic follows in a modern sans-serif with a welcoming c.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans: Expose is the compressed, refined one, with capitals barely rising above the lowercase, and it earns its keep big and short. Noto Sans is the sans-serif beneath, its lowercase filling most of the letter height.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Clean and contemporary, this body keeps its curve endings well apart and lets its lowercase c, s and z stand tall and full. Expose, compressed and striking, earns its keep big and short above it.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjoine: Professional and modern, this body leaves generous space between curve ends and stems, with little height difference between its cases. Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined handles steady reading in sans-serif, while Expose is the compressed, striking one that does its best work in headings.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hie: Expose has a compressed, refined cadence, its capitals sitting almost level with the lowercase. Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs follows in a plain sans whose x-height rises close to cap height, so a long page reads smoothly.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Striking and compressed, Expose barely pauses between letters. Noto Sans Arabic does the quieter work in sans, with wide openings on its small letters and a pronounced x-height that makes extended text comfortable.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Expose is compressed to the point of having almost no gap between lowercase and capitals, a refined, striking cadence. Noto Sans Armenian takes over in sans-serif with tall, full c, s and z, so text runs approachable for pages on end.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Professional and modern, this body gives every curved glyph a breathing space and keeps its ascenders short. Noto Sans Balinese would carry a long page without tiring, while Expose above it stays compressed and striking.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Modern and clean, this body lets its curved strokes end before turning inward and opens big counters in every small letter. And Expose, compressed and striking, does its best work up top, while the plain sans simply carries the text.
